t.7.19.1: Then, having conquered Marutta, that lord of the Rākṣasas, the ten-faced one, eager for battle, went forth to the cities of the kings of men.
t.7.19.2: Having approached those lords of kings, who were like great Indra and Varuṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas said, "Let battle be given to me!"
t.7.19.4: Then many wise kings, firm in their resolve upon dharma, knowing the boon-granted might of their foe, declared, "We are vanquished."
t.7.19.3: Or else declare, 'We have been conquered,' for this indeed is my resolve. Should you act otherwise, there will be no escape for you.
t.7.19.5: Duṣyanta, Suratha, Gādhi, Gaya and King Purūravas, all these rulers of the earth, dear child, declared, "We are vanquished."
t.7.19.6: Then Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, reached Ayodhyā, well guarded by Anaraṇya as Amarāvatī is guarded by Śakra.
t.7.19.7: Approaching the king, he said: "Let battle be given to me, or else say, 'I am conquered'; this is my command here."
t.7.19.8: Then Anaraṇya, greatly enraged, said to the lord of the Rākṣasas: "A single combat is granted to you by me, O sovereign of the Rākṣasas."
t.7.19.10: Many thousands of elephants and likewise ten thousand horses, together with foot soldiers and chariots, covering the earth, marched forth in an instant.
t.7.19.9: Then the very mighty army of that king, excellent and victorious, which had been readied beforehand by him who had heard the news, marched forth, intent on slaying the rākṣasa.
t.7.19.11: Then, O king, having come up against Rāvaṇa's army, the army of that lord of the earth perished like an oblation offered into the fire.
t.7.19.12: But that lord of men saw his mighty army perishing, like the waters of the five rivers vanishing on reaching the great ocean.
t.7.19.13: Then the lord of men, himself drawing his bow that resembled Śakra's bow, and overwhelmed with fury, advanced upon that Rāvaṇa.
t.7.19.14: Then the delight of the Ikṣvāku race rained eight hundred arrows down upon the head of that king of the Rākṣasas.
t.7.19.15: His arrows, as they fell, made no wound anywhere, like streams of water falling from the clouds upon a mountain's peak.
t.7.19.17: That king fell to the ground, his limbs overcome and trembling, like a mighty sāla tree in the forest that has fallen, scorched by a thunderbolt.
t.7.19.16: Then the king, struck on the head with the palm of the hand by the enraged lord of the rākṣasas, fell from his chariot and lay stretched out.
t.7.19.18: Laughing, the Rākṣasa said to him, the Ikṣvāku lord of the earth: "What fruit have you now gained by fighting against me?"
t.7.19.19: O lord of men, there is no one in the three worlds who could give me combat. I suspect that, lost in pleasures, you have not heard of my strength.
t.7.19.20: As he was speaking thus, the king, his life-breath ebbing, spoke these words: “What indeed can be done here, since Time is hard to overcome?”
t.7.19.21: Truly I have not been conquered by you, O Rākṣasa, you who praise yourself. Here I have perished by Time, and you are merely the instrument of my end.
t.7.19.23: If I have given gifts, if I have offered oblations, if my austerity has been well performed, if my subjects have been rightly protected, then may my word prove true.
t.7.19.22: But what can I do now, as my life ebbs away? Because you have insulted the Ikṣvākus, I shall speak these words, O Rākṣasa.
t.7.19.24: For in this very lineage of the great-souled Ikṣvākus there shall be born a king of supreme splendor, who will take away your life-breaths.
t.7.19.25: Then, when that curse had been pronounced, the drum of the gods was beaten, booming loud as a thundercloud, and a shower of flowers fell from the sky.
t.7.19.26: Then, O lord of kings, that king went to the abode of heaven; and when the king had gone to heaven, O Rāma, that Rākṣasa turned back.
